full_judgment:
Mr. Shahidul Islam, J.:- By this Rule the Opposite Parties were called upon to show cause as to why the impugned judgment... and decree dated 30.5.1992 passed by the .learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court; .Dhaka in Title Appeal No 1.23 of 1991 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 20.2.1991 passed by the learned Assistant, Judge, 5th Court; Dhaka in Title Suit No. 244 of 1999 decreeing the - suit should not be set aside and/ or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 4. The Assistant Judge upon consideration of the evidence on record decreed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 2U.1991. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 123of 1991. That appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge; 3rd Court Dhaka Who by the impugned judgment and decree dated 30.5.1992 dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment, and decree of the trial Court. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and .decree the defendant has obtained the instant Rule. 

 7. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Advocate for the Petitioner took me to the contract in question and submitted that Rahima Begum being the mother of minor defendant had no lawful right to enter into a contract for sale of the suit land. He submitted that mother being a defacto guardian of her minor son had no lawful authority to entered into a contract for sale without being authorized by Court of law. He submitted that the Courts below upon misconception of law and facts granted the plaintiffs prayer for Specific Performance of Contract against the settled principle of law. He submitted that the impugned judgment and decree are although based upon concurrent finding of fact but those having had passed against the law those are liable to be set aside by this Court. 

 11. Section 11 of the Contract Act enunciated the principle for entering a contract who ,is  competent to make a contract in section reads thus: "H. Who are competent to contract-Every person is competent to contract who is of the age of majority according to the law to which he is subject, and who is of sound mind: and is not disqualified from contracting by any law to which he is subject." A minor cannot enter a contract for sale of any land so also a mother of a, minor without being empowered from a Court of law cannot enter into a contract for transfer of land. That proposition finds support from the case law report in 1 PLR Dhaka 627. Following the decision in the case of Imam Bandi and Mir Shajahan a Division Bench of Patna High Court in the case of Abdul Huq -v- Md. Yusuf Khan, reported in 78 IC 483 refused Specific Performance of Contract for sale against minor and in that case Das, J observed as follows: "The defendant No. 2' as the defector guardian-of the defendant No. 3.and 4 had no power to convey the plaintiff the of the 'defendant No. 3 and 4 in the properties agreed to be sold". This principle or law is squarely application in the instant case. Our Appellate Division in the case of Acchang Proshad Nandy -v- Chilia Rashid and others, reported in 1982 BLD(AD)90 considered the question of Specific Performance of Contract entered into by two major and one minor defendants represented by mother who was her guardian appointed by the Court. In that case ultimately the contract of mother on behalf of her minor son was found to be void. The decision is also squarely applicable in the instant case. Section 22 of the Specific Relief Act is a bar in granting the relief as sought in the suit. In the case of Mehem Hossain and others-v-Nazrul Islam and others, reported in 46 DLR 86 it has been held that mother is not the legal guardian of the immovable property of a minor children though she may be in charge of the same. The position is no better than that of any other persons who has been the charge of persons or property of a minor and he is nothing but a "defacto guardian" having no power to 'convey to anything any right or interest in the immovable property. The whole case of the plaintiff if be accepted as a whole then there 'shall be no scope open before a Court of law for granting performance of the contract. In view of the above there is no hesitation on but that the alleged contract was a void contract in the eye of law. In view of the above both the Courts below have committed an error of law resulting in 'an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice in granting a relief against law and the judgment and decree impugned in this Rule is liable to be set aside. The rule is merits consideration. 

 12. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 30.5.1992 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 123 of 1991 dismissing the appeal and affirming those dated 20.2.1991 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 5'h Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 244 of 1999 is hereby set aside. The suit is dismissed without any order as to costs. The order of stay granted by this Court dated 2.9'.1992 is hereby vacated.
